result.journal: Journal of Urban Design and Light
result.keywords: This article examines how small municipalities coordinate decorative lighting schedules for public orchards and pedestrian corridors. A mixed-method approach is used to compare seasonal illumination plans, citizen feedback, and energy-use logs across several pilot neighborhoods. The study proposes a simple planning framework for balancing nighttime aesthetics, pollinator-friendly dark intervals, and maintenance constraints. Results suggest that phased lantern timing improves public satisfaction while reducing unnecessary power demand in community-managed green spaces.
result.title: Crescent Protocols for Orchard Lantern Schedules.
